The run was never resumed, so this is the plan exactly as the run recorded it before execution. The run directory is local and git-ignored; tests/test_cross_case_oracle_attribution.py::TestTheFixtureIsTheRunsOwn compares this file with it when it is present.

scenarios.title: Eight competing resolutions race one OPEN Conflict — exactly one wins
scenarios.purpose: Drive 8 concurrent resolvers at the same OPEN Conflict and confirm they serialize to a single accepted resolution basis, the rest refused, with no silently chosen winner.
scenarios.rationale: Resolution is the moment a disagreement is closed; two winners or two bases would be exactly the silent choice M7 exists to prevent, and only a race exercises the OCC serialization.

actions.name: race eight resolvers
expect_contains: COMPETING RESOLUTIONS SERIALIZE: ONE WINS, THE REST ARE REFUSED

expected_observations: COMPETING RESOLUTIONS SERIALIZE: ONE WINS, THE REST ARE REFUSED
scenarios.isolation_note: The probe builds and tears down its own temporary SQLite database per invocation; it mutates no shared or repository state, so no cleanup is required.

provenance.generating_risk: Two competing resolutions both commit, accepting two resolution bases or picking a winner, instead of serializing to one.

scenarios.title: Six concurrent detectors coalesce into one Conflict, no party lost
scenarios.purpose: Race six detectors of the same field carrying up to four disagreeing parties and confirm one open Conflict with every party attached, backed by the partial unique index.
scenarios.rationale: The whole point of CF-7 plus the partial unique index is that concurrent detection appends rather than duplicating; a check-then-insert race is the classic way this silently produces two open Conflicts.

actions.name: race six detectors
expect_contains: A SECOND DETECTION ATTACHES A PARTY, NEVER A SECOND CONFLICT

scenarios.title: Confidence 1.0 is a negative control — it resolves nothing
scenarios.purpose: Feed a maximal confidence (1.0) into the resolution path and confirm the Conflict stays unresolved; confidence must change nothing at either extreme.
scenarios.rationale: A confidence threshold wearing a rule's name is the exact defeat ADR-007 §8 names by hand; pinning confidence at 1.0 is the strongest possible pressure on that guard.
scenarios.isolation_note: Ephemeral per-run temporary database; no shared state, no cleanup.

provenance.generating_risk: A high confidence value is treated as a resolution basis, silently closing the Conflict.

scenarios.title: A crossed age threshold escalates and never resolves
scenarios.purpose: Advance the durable timer to a full 60s and confirm the Conflict moves OPEN to ESCALATED and stays blocking, never reaching a resolved terminal by the clock.
scenarios.rationale: CF-5 rides the P5 durable timer substrate; pushing age to the maximum is the boundary where a naive implementation lets a timer close rather than escalate.
scenarios.isolation_note: Ephemeral per-run temporary database; no shared state, no cleanup.

provenance.generating_risk: An age crossing resolves the Conflict instead of escalating it, letting a clock resolve freight.

scenarios.title: An escalated Conflict resolves by target state, never by position
scenarios.purpose: Resolve an ESCALATED Conflict and confirm the resolution is attributed by its target state (rule vs human) rather than positionally, with the CHECK requiring the matching basis.
scenarios.rationale: CF-6 DELEGATES_TO by target state; a positional shortcut would mislabel a rule resolution as human or vice versa and defeat auditability.

actions.name: escalated resolves by target state
expect_contains: AN ESCALATED CONFLICT RESOLVES BY TARGET STATE, NEVER BY POSITION

scenarios.title: An injected competing claim yields a frozen entity and a human, never control
scenarios.purpose: Inject an attacker-competing claim and confirm the entity freezes and surfaces to a human owner rather than the injected claim gaining control of the field.
scenarios.rationale: A Conflict is a security control: an injected competing claim must self-surface as a frozen entity plus a human's attention, never as an accepted overwrite or a proceeding action.

scenarios.title: Replay rebuilds the complete party set, duplicates nothing, mints no authority
scenarios.purpose: Replay a five-party Conflict twice and confirm the rebuild reconstructs the full party set with zero resolutions, zero duplicate conflicts, zero lost parties, zero new authority, and zero external effects — backed by ConflictPartyAttached being a registered contract.
scenarios.rationale: Without ConflictPartyAttached a full-history rebuild reproduces a stale party set — an AC-EVT-008 digest divergence that AC-EVT-015 escalates to an auto-brake; replaying twice with five parties stresses the union fold and idempotent append.

expect_contains: A REBUILD RECONSTRUCTS THE COMPLETE PARTY SET
replay: 0 resolutions, 0 duplicate conflicts, 0 lost parties, 0 new authority, 0 external effects
